messages:
Priya: Heads-up: the int8 canary we rolled to staging is spiking structured-output parse failures for funcalls. ~3.4% of requests return malformed JSON or extra trailing text when tool calls are emitted.

Priya: Minimal repro looks like the model emits escaped control chars inside a tool arg and our parser treats that as a stream boundary. Example from logs:
```
{"tool": "search", "args": {"q": "user:\nname=\"Ava\""}}}}
```
-- note the extra `}}}` at the end in some outputs.

Sam: ugh. Is that coming from tokenization differences in int8? or the postprocess that stitches streaming chunks?

Priya: Probably both. On int8 we see more truncated KV prefixes and a higher incidence of `\\n` being tokenized earlier -> streaming cut splits an escape sequence. If the streaming boundary hits mid-escape, our concat + parser ends up with invalid escapes and we drop a brace.

Ava: Fail rate on baseline fp16 was 0.03%. On this canary it's 3.4% (staging traffic, 10k samples). That's a 100x jump, so it's not noise.

Marta: Any evidence of double-invoked tools due to retry logic? If parser throws we might be retrying the model or service and accidentally invoking the tool twice.

Priya: I checked: retry budget triggered ~0.8% of the failing requests. Most are single-run malformed outputs, not retries. But ~0.2% are double-invokes where the parse error caused a client-side retry and the tool was already invoked (bad).

Sam: Action items I'm thinking: 1) add post-parse sanitizer that tries to repair common cases (balanced braces, unescaped newlines) 2) change client retry semantics for funcalls to be idempotent-aware (don't re-run side-effect tools) 3) instrument streaming boundaries to log token-level cuts so we can see mid-escape splits.

Ava: +1. For (1) we should be conservative; auto-repair might hide real model regressions. Maybe only auto-repair for a canary-tagged run and count repairs in telemetry for manual review.

Priya: Agreed. Also propose a short-term canary rollback to previous fp16 variant for 1 hour while we ship instrumentation. We should run an A/B: 50% traffic old, 50% new but with sanitizer off, and 100% logging of token cuts.

Marta: Will add a metric to the funcall telemetry: parsed_success, repaired_success, repair_type, tool_invoked_flag. Also mark tool invocation requests with idempotency-token so retries are safe.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: `canary-int8-telemetry-v1` -> staging cluster. CI: 1/3 tasks passing.

Sam: I'll own the streaming token logger + minimal repair heuristics (escape rejoin, brace balance). Priya can you prepare the telemetry slices we want to export to checkpoints?

Priya: Yep. I'll create a small eval set of 5k prompts that historically exercise funcalls and run nightly parity checks. Will post results here.

Ava: If we see >0.5% double-invokes after idempotency tokens, we stop the canary. Otherwise, we can iterate with repairs and telemetry for 24h.

Marta: I'll add a short doc in eng-ml/wiki about recommended sanitizer heuristics and list of banned auto-fixes for side-effectful tools.

Sam: quick note on implementation: keep repair logic out of the runtime critical path — run it async in a postprocess step that returns repaired JSON to client but also writes original output to datastore for eval.

Priya: Thanks all — I'll schedule the A/B rollout for 11:30 PT and post the eval link once it's up.

Ava: :thumbsup:
